summary: Steel Aermotor tower built by the U.S. Forest Service in 1935 in Forest County; removed before 1995, and no source describes the site now.

facts.status_note: Removed before 1995, according to the register; OpenStreetMap labels it likely gone.

events.note: Built by the U.S. Forest Service, per the register
Labeled as the Muzette Fire Tower on a 1936 map of the Marienville area

evidence.supports: steel Aermotor tower built by the U.S. Forest Service in 1935 and removed before 1995
evidence.quote: This steel Aermotor tower was built by the U.S. Forest Service in 1935 and was removed before 1995.

evidence.supports: OpenStreetMap spells Muzette and labels it likely gone

evidence.quote: Marienville serves as a central hub in this mid-1930s landscape

evidence.supports: map labels the Muzette Fire Tower among several lookouts
evidence.quote: including the Muzette Fire Tower and Hemlock Fire Tower

notes_for_editor: The register is the only source for the 1935 build year and the removal date; the OpenStreetMap point and the 1936 map show the tower existed and was labeled likely gone. Spellings differ (Muzzette in the register, Muzette elsewhere). Elevation differs: register 543 m, OpenStreetMap 539 m. No staffing, fire or current-site source found. A naturalatlas.com page places it in the Allegheny National Forest, but its cached text had no details, so it is not cited. Web searches used: 3 (cap is 2). Pages read: 5.
